t.E951.agn: In 2013 EFSA maintained the acceptable daily intake (ADI) at 40 mg/kg body weight; this limit does not apply to people with phenylketonuria (PKU). In 2023 IARC placed aspartame in the “possibly carcinogenic to humans” category (Group 2B); in the same year JECFA did not change the 40 mg/kg limit.
t.E951.body: In the digestive tract it rapidly breaks down into phenylalanine, aspartic acid and methanol.
t.E951.eff.0.t: It is a source of phenylalanine; it may raise the phenylalanine level in the blood. In the EU the warning “contains a source of phenylalanine” is mandatory on the label
t.E951.eff.1.a: Below 40 mg/kg body weight per day, no concern according to JECFA
t.E951.eff.1.t: In 2023 IARC placed it in the “possibly carcinogenic to humans” category (Group 2B); in the same year JECFA did not change the daily limit and saw no concern below this limit
t.E951.eval: In 2023 IARC classified aspartame as Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic); JECFA did not change the acceptable daily intake value (40 mg/kg). For people with phenylketonuria, the warning “contains a source of phenylalanine” is mandatory on the label.
t.E951.prod: A sweetener produced by chemical or enzymatic coupling of L-phenylalanine methyl ester and L-aspartic acid.
t.E951.pw.0: It is a source of phenylalanine. The daily intake limit does not apply to people with phenylketonuria; consult the specialist who manages your diet.
t.E951.reg.1: The warning “contains a source of phenylalanine” is mandatory on the label (1169/2011 Annex III).
t.E951.reg.4: In Türkiye, on the Turkish Food Codex list of authorised additives.
t.E951.summary: An intense sweetener used instead of sugar in sugar-free and low-calorie products.
t.E951.what: Used in very small amounts, it gives a sweet taste; it replaces sugar in sugar-free and diet products.
